2. Confirmat me quoque in eâ sententiâ
tempestatis ratio, qui enim Herodis mortem in ultima Ianuarii
aut martii conjiciunt, coguntur statuere, haud multis
post eclipsin diebus Herodem ad thermas Callirrhoes
deductum, spe levaminis acquirendi. Ita Herodes
media brumâ aut eâ exeunte usus fuisset thermis, quod
ab omni lege & prudentiâ medicâ absonum est. Quis
enim Medicus parum prudentior homini, jam tum pericu-
losè aegrotanti, & senecture [?] propemodum confecto,
thermas praescripserit, tanto itinere adeundas, brumâ vi-
gente, aut nondum praeterlapsâ quarum usus elementio-
rem aëris temperiem postulat; ut haud dubitandum vide-
atur Herodem thermis usum fuisse non brumali, sed
autumnali anni tempestate. Sanè poros corporis largioris
sudoris profluvio recludere, quando aëtheris frigidi-
oris praedominium obtinet, atque ita ab usu therma-
rum attenuatum senis corpusculum ita reclusum iniqui-
ori ambientis aëris rigori exponere, non esse Medico-
rum indicationibus consentaneum, assentiertur [?] mihi cre-
do quilibet rei medicae peritus.

page.notes: The first line of the page continues a sentence from the previous page, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". The printed hyphens at the line ends ("tem-porique", "frigidi-oris", "iniqui-ori") are kept. Long s is transcribed as plain s (e.g. "frustra", "existimarunt", "praeterlapsâ"). "senecture" is doubtful and marked [?]; the printed form may be "senectute". "assentiertur" is printed as such and may be a misprint for "assentientur"; left as printed and marked [?]. "XLII" is printed in small capitals as "xlii". The signature "P" is taken as printed without a number.
